entries.label: In lieu of a required cover letter, please describe why you are interested in interning at Hudl in 2-5 sentences.
entries.value: Most of what I've built has pushed me toward testing and evaluation as the harder half of the problem. At Intelehealth I designed an evaluation framework for AI-generated clinical outputs against a 4,169-case benchmark, using stratified sampling to surface systematic failure modes rather than reporting a single accuracy number, and that work convinced me that deciding whether an output should be trusted is usually harder than producing it. In my own Playwright-based application agent I built a validation ladder (unit, fixture, live read-only, live mutation) because I didn't want the system calling a capability "working" just because it passed against a local fixture, and I put every mutating action behind fail-closed flags. Hudl is interesting to me because it's software real teams depend on during real games, where a bug isn't abstract, and QA is where I'd get to think hardest about failure modes on a product that actually gets used.
